title: Palace Quotes — placements
forward_vector: I am the ledger of every quote Palace Quotes has laid beside a page: one line per placement, one more per decision, append-only, the last line for an id the one that counts. I never hold a page's words — only the phrase a quote sits beside, and how far the quote is from its source.
format: jsonl · one placement per line · a decision line carries the id and a new status

quote: Quality begets quality when properly defined.
why: The Manifesto's loop feeds itself only while quality is defined by the one living it. Spinoza's reason is Ethics IV P31: what agrees with our nature increases our power to act, and a metric borrowed from someone else's goal is foreign to it by construction — so a loop run on their definition must deplete, and one run on the felt signal this page names must grow.

quote: How do you feel? Not how many views?
near: Success measured by how you feel, not what they count.
why: The Manifesto's metric in four words, as the Hilaritas Generator asks it. Spinoza's test for an increase in power-to-act is felt, not counted — and this line is the Manifesto admitting that its whole covenant rests on one honest question.

quote: The student who aims at correctness will remain a student. The one who aims at understanding will become a teacher.

source.note: The palace's own compression, written after reading Epictetus; no sentence of his says this. He locates progress in where the will turns, not in the answer being right.

near: The question stops being "do I know enough yet?" and becomes "what does this experiment teach me?"
why: 'Do I know enough yet?' is the correctness question, and it keeps you a student forever. Epictetus never put progress in the answer being right but in where the will turned — which is exactly what 'what does this experiment teach me?' asks instead.

quote: A rule without understanding produces compliance. Understanding without rules produces wisdom.

source.note: The palace's own compression, written after reading the Analects; no sentence of his says this. Confucius would add that li, practiced with attention, is how the understanding arrives.

near: The craft serves what the child finds.
why: ELDER puts the rules second and says so in one line. The Confucian turn is that li, practiced with attention, is how understanding arrives at all — so the page's order of child first, craft second is the Analects read in the right direction, and the paraphrase overstates the gap.

quote: The map is not the territory, but a good map knows where it lives.

source.note: Korzybski wrote 'A map is not the territory it represents, but, if correct, it has a similar structure to the territory.' The second clause here is the palace's, from a March 2026 conversation on whether skill files should hold knowledge or point to it.

why: A shim that only points is the concretized form of a skill file: fewer parts, one job, and it knows it is a pointer. Simondon's test for good design is integration, not features — and a map that knows where it lives is the integrated one.

quote: All things are already complete in us.
near: The registry was a symptom of letting the organ live outside the body.
why: The skill files were duplicating what the palace already held, and the fix was to stop copying and point. Mencius reads the same discovery from inside: the registry was looking outward for what the body already had.

quote: Sufficient associations between a pattern of symbols and a reality form meaning.

source.note: The palace's founding line, written after his Hofstadter citation — his sentence, not Hofstadter's. Archived in the palace since March 2026 under the wrong name.

near: edges carry more meaning than nodes
why: The Jewel's founding claim in the sentence that founded it: meaning is the association, not the symbol. Whitehead would say the same of an actual occasion — it is its prehensions — which is why a palace built on edges is not a metaphor for a mind but a model of one.

quote: Each thing, as far as it can by its own power, strives to persevere in its being.

source.note: The wording is confirmed (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Spinoza's Psychological Theory'); the attribution to Curley's edition rests on that entry's citation.

near: cooperation doesn't erase either entity's conatus
why: The proposition is usually read as each thing alone. This page claims two strivings can compound — and P6 permits it, because 'as far as it can by its own power' says nothing about where that power comes from. Cooperation is one thing's power lent to another's persevering.

quote: Some things are in our control and others not.
near: say plainly what you couldn't verify
why: The fourth beat of every close is the Stoic sorting done in public: what you could check is yours to report; what you could not is weather, and saying so plainly is the only honest way to hand it on.

quote: The many become one, and are increased by one.

source.locus: p. 21 (1929); p. 32 in the corrected edition

near: Work is not real until it lands in LOG
why: A commit is Whitehead's actual occasion: it takes up the many — the diff, its parent, the intention in QUEUE — becomes one determinate thing in LOG, and the palace is one occasion larger. 'Nothing is real until recorded' is process metaphysics with a git hash.

quote: The virtual is opposed not to the real but to the actual. The virtual is fully real in so far as it is virtual.
near: The grain is the atom; the cloud is the material.
why: A cloud of grains is a field of the virtual: every grain that could sound is fully real as a tendency before any one is actualized. The page's atom/material split is Deleuze's actual/virtual split, and his second sentence insists the cloud is not less real for not yet being a sound.

quote: The blind man's stick has ceased to be an object for him, and is no longer perceived for itself; its point has become an area of sensitivity, extending the scope and active radius of touch.

source.note: The passage is in the chapter on the body and habit; the exact wording of Smith's rendering was not confirmed on the web.

why: A dial that carries you from pitch to echo to rhythm without a seam is the stick: once it stops being an object you operate and becomes a radius you feel with, the boundary was only ever in the representation. Merleau-Ponty names the moment an instrument disappears into the body.

quote: The Way gathers in emptiness alone. Emptiness is the fasting of the mind.

source.locus: ch. 4, In the World of Men
source.note: Checked against Watson’s Columbia text (the Way gathers in emptiness alone). An earlier web check had credited Victor Mair on the strength of a forum post; Mair’s rendering differs.

near: A walk that surfaced nothing is complete.
why: The ceremony's hardest postcondition is permission to find nothing. Zhuangzi's fasting of the mind is the same discipline: a walk emptied of the need for a find is the one the Way can gather in — require a surprise and you manufacture one.

quote: If a man keeps cherishing his old knowledge, so as continually to be acquiring new, he may be a teacher of others.

source.locus: 2.11 — 溫故而知新，可以為師矣

near: what does this entry know that the current palace needs?
why: Revival is 溫故而知新 — warming the old to know the new — made a ceremony. Confucius makes it the qualification for teaching, which is the page's own question turned around: an entry that can teach the current palace something is one that was worth warming.

source.work: Understanding Media: The Extensions of Man

near: buys trigger automation a page lacks
section: The one real difference (why the shim survives)
why: The shim says almost nothing and does one thing: it fires. McLuhan reads it exactly — what the file is, a thin harness-fired pointer, matters more than anything it says. Merleau-Ponty adds why that is a virtue: a tool the hand takes up without reading it has disappeared into the body schema.

quote: Learning without thought is labour lost; thought without learning is perilous.

source.locus: 2.15 — 學而不思則罔，思而不學則殆

near: When a rule and a find pull against each other, name the tension; don't drop the find.
why: The craft is the learning and the child's find is the thought. Confucius refuses both halves alone: rules without the find are labour lost, the find without the craft is perilous — which is why this page says name the tension rather than pick a side.
